title: Calgary SPV-002 BlazeMaster CPVC in residential partial-flow-through fire sprinkler systems

facts.text: The Calgary variance is dated July 15, 2018 and identifies NPC 2015 Division B Clauses 2.6.2.4(2)(a) and 2.2.5.8 as the applicable regulatory requirements.
The stated scope is BlazeMaster CPVC pipe in residential partial-flow-through fire sprinkler/standpipe system applications using a DuCF backflow preventer.

The variance says the then-current product did not meet the cited NPC 2015 requirements and describes a conditional fallback: if Lubrizol's CSA project P-17-13 were rejected, DCVAF devices were to be installed and tested for the covered installations in Calgary.

The document makes the variance applicable to the building/plumbing permit address when SPV-002 is referenced in the permit conditions, and requires the owner/contractor to carry out the project as outlined.

Calgary's 2023 product advisory describes testing, certification, evaluation, qualification, and an alternative-solution path for products under NBC(AE), and describes alternative solutions as site- and project-specific; it does not discuss SPV-002 or the NPC 2015 clauses.
Calgary's 2023 variance guide says variances are not intended as general product or equipment approvals.

limitations: This is an issued variance, not an application or test report.
The document refers to a manufacturer/CSA standards change project; this research did not verify that project's later outcome or current product status.
The Calgary current SPV index does not list SPV-002, although the direct official PDF remained downloadable; current posting/validity is not inferred.
B23-014 addresses NBC(AE) materials and systems guidance and is attached for context only; it does not establish a current NPC permission.
